paragraphs.text: The Acts of Peter and Andrew

It came to pass when Andrew the apostle of Christ went forth from the city of the man-eaters, behold a luminous cloud snatched him up, and carried him away to the mountain where Peter and Matthew and Alexander were sitting. And when he saw them, they saluted him with great joy. Then Peter says to him: What has happened to you, brother Andrew? Have you sown the word of truth in the country of the man-eaters or not? Andrew says to him: Yes, father Peter, through your prayers; but the men of that city have done me many mischiefs, for they dragged me through their street three days, so that my blood stained the whole street. Peter says to him: Be a man in the Lord, brother Andrew, and come hither, and rest from your labour. For if the good husbandman laboriously till the ground, it will also bear fruit, and straightway all his toil will be turned into joy; but if he toil, and his land bring forth no fruit, he has double toil.

And while he was thus speaking, the Lord Jesus Christ appeared to them in the form of a child, and said to them: Hail, Peter, bishop of the whole of my Church! Hail, Andrew! My co-heirs, be courageous, and struggle for mankind; for verily I say unto you, you shall endure toils in this world for mankind. But be bold; I will give you rest in one hour of repose in the kingdom of my Father. Arise, then, and go into the city of the barbarians, and preach in it; and I will be with you in the wonders that shall happen in it by your hands. And the Lord Jesus, after saluting them, went up into the heavens in glory.

And Peter, and Andrew, and Alexander, and Rufus, and Matthias, went into the city of the barbarians. And after they had come near the city, Andrew answered and said to Peter: Father Peter, have we again to undergo toils in this city, as in the country of the man-eaters? Peter says to him: I do not know. But, behold, there is an old man before us sowing in his field: if we go up to him, let us say to him, Give us bread; and if he give us bread, we may know that we are not to suffer in this city; but if he say to us, We have no bread, on the other hand, we shall know that suffering again awaits us. And when they came up to the old man, Peter says to him: Hail, farmer! And the farmer says to them: Hail you too, merchants! Peter says to him: Have you bread to give to these children, for we have been in want? The old man says to them: Wait a little, and look after the oxen, and the plough, and the land, that I may go into the city, and get you loaves. Peter says to him: If you provide hospitality for us, we shall took after the cattle and the field. The old man says: So be it. Peter says to him: Are the oxen your own? The old man says: No; I have them on hire. Peter says to him: Go into the city. And the old man went into the city. And Peter arose, and girded up his cloak and his under-garment, and says to Andrew: It is not right for us to rest and be idle; above all, when the old man is working for us, having left his own work. Then Peter took hold of the plough, and sowed the wheat. And Andrew was behind the oxen, and says to Peter: Father Peter, why do you bring toil upon us, especially when we have work enough already! Then Andrew took the plough out of Peter's hand, and sowed the wheat, saying: O seed cast into the ground in the field of the righteous, come up, and come to the light. Let the young men of the city therefore come forth, whom I found in the pit of destruction until today; for, behold, the apostles of Christ are coming into the city, pardoning the sins of those who believe in them, and healing every disease, and every sickness. Pray ye for me, that He may have mercy upon me, and that I may be delivered from this strait.

And many of the multitude believed in Christ, because of the saying of the woman; and they fell at the feet of the apostles, and adored them. And they laid their hands upon them. And they healed those in the city that were sick, and gave sight to the blind and, hearing to the deaf, and drove out the demons. All the multitude glorified the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

And there was a certain rich man in the city, by name Onesiphorus. He, having seen the miracles done by the apostles, says to them: If I believe in your God, can I also do a miracle like you? Andrew says to him: If you will forsake all that belongs to you, and your wife and your children, as we also have done, then thou also shall do miracles. When Onesiphorus heard this, he was filled with rage, and took his scarf and threw it over Andrew's neck, and struck him, and said to him: You are a sorcerer. How do you force me to abandon my wife, and my children, and my goods? Then Peter, having turned and seen him striking Andrew, says to him: Man, stop now striking Andrew. Onesiphorus says to him: I see that you are more sensible than he. Do thou then tell me to leave my wife, and my children, and my goods. What do you say? Peter says to him: One thing I say unto you: it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to go into the kingdom of heaven. When Onesiphorus heard this, he was even more filled with rage and anger, and took his scarf off the neck of Andrew, and threw it upon the neck of Peter; and so he dragged him along, saying: Verily you are a great sorcerer, more than the other; for a camel cannot go through the eye of a needle. But if you wilt show me this miracle, I will believe in your God; and not only I, but also the whole city. But if not, you shall be grievously punished in the midst of the city. And when Peter heard this, he was exceedingly grieved, and stood and stretched forth his hands towards heaven, and prayed, saying: O Lord our God, listen to me at this time; for they will ensnare us from Your own words: for no prophet has spoken to set forth this his explanation, and no patriarch that we might learn the interpretation of it; and now we seek for ourselves the explanation with boldness. Do not then, Lord, overlook us: for you are He who is praised by the cherubim.

And after he had said this, the Saviour appeared in the form of a child of twelve years old, wearing a linen garment; and He says to them: Be courageous, and tremble not, my chosen disciples; for I am with you always. Let the needle and the camel be brought. And after saying this, He went up into the heavens. And there was a certain merchant in the city who had believed in the Lord through the Apostle Philip; and when he heard of this, he ran and searched for a needle with a big eye, to do a favour to the apostles. When Peter learned this, he said: My son, do not search for a big needle; for nothing is impossible with God: rather bring us a small needle. And after the needle had been brought, and all the multitude of the city were standing by to see, Peter looked up and saw a camel coming. And he ordered her to be brought. Then he fixed the needle in the ground, and cried out with a loud voice, saying: In the name of Jesus Christ, who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, I order you, O camel, to go through the eye of the needle. Then the eye of the needle was opened like a gate, and the camel went through it, and all the multitude saw it. Again Peter says to the camel: Go again through the needle. And the camel went a second time. When Onesiphorus saw this, he said to Peter; Truly you are a great sorcerer; but I do not believe unless I send and bring a camel and a needle. And he called one of his servants, and said to him privately: Go and bring me here a camel and a needle; find also a polluted woman, and force her to come here: for these men are sorcerers. And Peter having learned the mystery through the Spirit, says to Onesiphorus: Send and bring the camel, and the woman, and the needle. And when they brought them, Peter took the needle, and fixed it in the ground. And the woman was sitting on the camel. Then Peter says: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ the crucified, I order you, O camel, to go through this needle. And immediately the eye of the needle was opened, and became like a gate, and the camel went through it. Peter again says to the camel: Go through it again, that all may see the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ, in order that some may believe in Him. Then the camel again went through the needle. And Onesiphorus seeing it, cried out, and said: Truly great is the God of Peter and Andrew, and I from this time forth believe in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Now then, hear my words, O Peter. I have grain lands, vineyards, and fields; I have also twenty-seven pounds of gold, and fifty pounds of silver; and I have very many slaves. I give my possessions to the poor, that I also may do one miracle like you. And Peter was grieved lest the powers should not work in him, seeing that he had not received the seal in Christ. And while he was considering this, behold, a voice out of the heaven saying to him: Do to him what he wishes, because I will accomplish for him what he desires. latex.p0002: \Emph{源自牛津大学博德利图书馆抄本。}
latex.p0003: 当基督的宗徒安德肋离开食人者的城市时，看，一朵发光的云将他卷起，带到伯多禄、玛窦和亚历山大所在的山上。他一看见他们，他们便满心欢喜地向他请安。于是伯多禄对他说：\Quote{安德肋兄弟，你遭遇了何事？你在食人者的地域是否播下了真理之言？}安德肋对他说：\Quote{是的，伯多禄父，藉着你的祈祷；但那城的人对我行了诸多恶事，因为他们拖着我在他们的街市上走了三天，以致我的血染遍了整条街道。}伯多禄对他说：\Quote{安德肋兄弟，你要在主内作大丈夫，到这里来，从你的劳苦中休息。因为，好农夫若辛勤耕耘土地，土地就会结出果实，他的一切辛劳便立即化为喜乐；但若他辛劳，他的土地却不结果实，那他就有了双重的辛劳。}
latex.p0004: 他正这样说时，主耶稣基督以孩童的形象显现给他们，对他们说：\Quote{你们好，伯多禄，我整个教会的主教！你好，安德肋！我的同承继人，要勇敢，为人类奋斗；因为我实在告诉你们：你们要在这世上为人类忍受辛劳。\Emph{但要勇敢；我将在一次安息中的休息里，在我父的王国中赐予你们安息。}那么，起来，进入外邦人的城市，在那里宣讲；我必与你们同在，藉着你们的手在那里发生的奇事中。}主耶稣向他们请安后，光荣地升天去了。
latex.p0005: 伯多禄、安德肋、亚历山大、鲁富、玛弟亚便进入外邦人的城市。他们走近城门时，安德肋回答伯多禄说：\Quote{伯多禄父，我们还要在这城里像在食人者的地域一样，再遭受辛劳吗？}伯多禄对他说：\Quote{我不知道。但看，我们面前有一位老人正在地里撒种：若我们到他那里去，对他说\InnerQuote{给我们饼}；若他给了我们饼，我们就知道在这城里不会受苦；但若他对我们说\InnerQuote{我们没有饼}，那么，我们就知道苦难又在等待我们。}他们来到老人跟前，伯多禄对他说：\Quote{农夫，你好！}农夫对他们说：\Quote{你们商人也好！}伯多禄对他说：\Quote{你有饼给这些孩子吗？因为我们缺乏食物。}老人对他们说：\Quote{稍等片刻，看管好牛、犁和地，我进城去给你们拿些饼来。}伯多禄对他说：\Quote{你若款待我们，我们就照管牲畜和田地。}老人说：\Quote{就这样吧。}伯多禄对他说：\Quote{这牛是你自己的吗？}老人说：\Quote{不是，我是租来的。}伯多禄对他说：\Quote{你进城去吧。}老人便进了城。伯多禄起来，束上外衣和内衣，对安德肋说：\Quote{我们不应休息和闲散，尤其当老人为我们劳作，撇下了他自己的工作。}于是伯多禄握住犁，撒下麦种。安德肋跟在牛后面，对伯多禄说：\Quote{伯多禄父，你为什么给我们增添辛苦，尤其我们本已工作够多了！}然后安德肋从伯多禄手中接过犁，撒下麦种，说：\Quote{哦，种子，撒在义人田间的地里，发芽吧，来到光明中。因此，那城中的青年们，我今日在毁灭的深坑中寻获的你们，都出来吧；因为，看，基督的宗徒们正进入城中，赦免那信从他们之人的罪，治愈各种疾病和各种灾殃。请为我祈祷，使祂怜悯我，使我脱离这困境。}
latex.p0006: 许多群众因那妇人的话而信了基督；他们俯伏在宗徒们脚前，朝拜他们。宗徒们便给他们覆手。他们治好了城中患病的人，使瞎子看见，聋子听见，驱逐了魔鬼。全体群众都光荣了父、及子、及圣神。
latex.p0007: 城中有一个富人，名叫敖乃息佛洛。他看见了宗徒们所行的奇迹，便对他们说：\Quote{我若信你们的天主，也能像你们一样行奇迹吗？}安德肋对他说：\Quote{你若舍弃你所拥有的一切，以及你的妻子儿女，如同我们所行的一样，那么你也能行奇迹。}敖乃息佛洛听了这话，满怀怒气，便解下他的围巾，套在安德肋的颈上，打了他，对他说：\Quote{你是行邪术的。你为什么强迫我舍弃我的妻子、儿女和财产？}伯多禄转身看见他打安德肋，便对他说：\Quote{人哪，现在住手，别再打安德肋了。}敖乃息佛洛对他说：\Quote{我看你比他更有见识。那么你告诉我，要我离开我的妻子、儿女和财产。你怎么说？}伯多禄对他说：\Quote{我对你说一件事：\InnerQuote{骆驼穿过针眼，比富人进入天国还容易。}}敖乃息佛洛听了这话，更是满怀怒气和愤恨，便从他的颈上取下围巾，套在伯多禄的颈上，就这样拖着他走，说：\Quote{你实在是个大行邪术的，比那人更甚；因为骆驼不可能穿过针眼。但倘若你愿向我显示这个奇迹，我就信你的天主；不但我，全城的人也都信。否则，你必在城中央受重罚。}伯多禄听了这话，极其忧伤，便站着向天伸出双手，祈祷说：\Quote{主、我们的天主，求祢此时垂听我；因为他们要从祢自己的话中陷害我们：因为没有一个先知说话提出过祂的解释，也没有一个圣祖使我们能学到它的释义；现在我们自己大胆寻求解释。主，求祢不要忽略我们：因为祢是那受革鲁宾赞美者。}
latex.p0008: 祂说了这话以后，救主以十二岁孩童的形像显现，身穿细麻衣，对他们说：\Quote{你们要勇敢，不要战栗，我特选的门徒们，因为我常与你们同在。把针和骆驼带来。}说了这话，祂就升到天上。城里有一个商人，曾藉宗徒\Person{斐理伯}相信了主；他听见这事，就跑去寻找一支大眼的针，好为宗徒们效劳。\Person{伯多禄}知道后便说：\Quote{我儿，不要找大针，因为在天主没有不可能的事：给我们拿一支小针来罢。}针拿来后，全城的人都站着观看，\Person{伯多禄}举目看见一头骆驼前来，就吩咐把它牵来。然后把针插入地里，大声呼喊说：\Quote{我因耶稣基督之名——祂曾在\Person{般雀比拉多}手下被钉十字架——命令你，骆驼，穿过这针眼。}于是针眼像门一样张开，骆驼穿了过去，众人都看见了。\Person{伯多禄}又对骆驼说：\Quote{再穿过针一次。}骆驼便第二次穿了过去。\Person{敖乃西佛若}看见这事，对\Person{伯多禄}说：\Quote{你实在是个大术士；但除非我派人带来骆驼和针，否则我不相信。}他叫来一个仆人，私下对他说：\Quote{去给我带一头骆驼和一支针来；还要找一个不洁的妇人，强迫她到这里来，因为这些人都是术士。}\Person{伯多禄}藉着圣神知道了这奥秘，就对\Person{敖乃西佛若}说：\Quote{你派去把骆驼、妇人和针带来罢。}他们带齐后，\Person{伯多禄}拿起针，插入地里。妇人正骑在骆驼上。\Person{伯多禄}便说：\Quote{我因我们的主耶稣基督——被钉十字架者——之名，命令你，骆驼，穿过这支针。}针眼立刻张开，像门一样，骆驼穿了过去。\Person{伯多禄}又对骆驼说：\Quote{再穿过去，使众人看见我们的主耶稣基督的光荣，好叫一些人信从祂。}于是骆驼再次穿过针眼。\Person{敖乃西佛若}看见，就大声说：\Quote{伯多禄和安德肋的天主真是伟大！我从今以后信从我们的主耶稣基督之名。\Person{伯多禄}，现在请听我的话。我有谷田、葡萄园和农田，还有二十七磅金子和五十磅银子，还有许多奴隶。我把我的财产施舍给穷人，好使我也能像你一样行一个奇迹。}\Person{伯多禄}心里忧伤，怕那些能力不在他内运行，因为他还未接受基督内的印记。他正在思虑这事时，忽然有声音从天上对他说：\Quote{他愿意什么，你就为他做什么，因为他所愿的，我要为他成就。}\Person{伯多禄}对他说：\Quote{我儿，到这里来，照我们所做的去做。}\Person{敖乃西佛若}上前，站在骆驼和针前，说：\Quote{因……}\EditorialNote{手稿在此突然中断}
